europmc-pmc6879498: Zinc cells are cheap and safe - but their ends act up. This study built a zinc-friendly solid skin in place by tuning how ions swim. The protective layer extends battery life. Better zinc ends for grid-scale storage. The chemistry could make renewables more storable.
europmc-pmc6889398: 10,000 DNA sets remap life's oldest branches. This family-tree study of 10,575 bacteria and archaea DNA sets found deep closeness between the realms Bacteria and Archaea. The tree of life gets a major trim. Two realms, nearer kin than we thought.
europmc-pmc6938598: Adding chemo to hormone care helps - but for whom? This STAMPEDE study tried adding chemo to hormone care in low- and high-load spread prostate cancer. The load split steers care. Long-term results, cleanly split. High-load cases gain the most.
europmc-pmc6941098: miRNAs get tweaked - and their marks change. This review cracks miRNA action through miRNA editing: the after-copy turn. The tweakers retype control. A-to-I editing remolds gene control. Small tweaks, big fallout for ills. The review maps a new control layer.
europmc-pmc6963998: A plain blood ratio flags heart risk. This review tours the triglyceride-glucose index (TyG) in heart ills cases: the insulin defiance stand-in. The bargain fortune ball. Insulin defiance, cheap gauged. CAD risk sorting on a shoestring. The index merits clinic notice.
europmc-pmc7000698: Dying cells send messages in bubble bottles. This review tours dying-cell bubble messages from dying cells via outside-cell sacs. The death mail. Scripted death frees sac load. Dying-cell husks and tiny sacs known. Bubble release fresh accepted. Sound and sick roles probed.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1198: This 2007 GAO report wades into the drug-patent fight: a world trade pact lets poor nations break patents in a health crisis, but U.S. guidance on the deal read murky. GAO says Washington's line may need sharpening. The report sits at the crossroads of pill profits and sick patients half a world away.
gao-gaoreports-b-299798: Savantage Financial Services fought a 2007 award at GAO — two case numbers, one verdict. The firm said the agency's pick was unfair; the combined ruling weighs each protest point. Money-management contracts get the same fair-play scrutiny as any federal buy.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-498: The polar weather satellites were being rebuilt mid-flight in 2007 — GAO's report says the restructuring moved ahead despite technical storms. The findings track the high-wire act. The report's tension: fix the plane while flying it, or lose the forecast.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-98: Veterans' disability claims needed faster records in 2007, and GAO's report says the VA could improve how it got military service files. The findings target the delays. The report warns that the wounded should not wait on paperwork. The files had to follow the veteran.
gao-gaoreports-b-298698: General Electrodynamics Corporation doubled its November 2006 protest — two case numbers, one tech fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both. The firm challenged the awards, and the call weighs each claim. Paired filings get one careful answer. Two dockets, one fair verdict.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-798: Consumer-directed health plans got an early review in 2006, and GAO's report shares enrollees' experiences with the savings accounts and plans. The findings take the measure. The report warns that the do-it-yourself health funds needed watching. The plans had to work.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-498: The National Guard's civil support teams needed a clearer mission in 2006, and GAO's report says the bureau had to clarify their role and address management challenges. The findings demand the definition. The report warns that the homeland helpers needed a sharp mission. The mission had to be clear.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-298: State Department travel billing lost taxpayer money in 2006, and GAO's report says control breakdowns and weak oversight were to blame. The findings follow the waste. The report warns that the diplomats' travel tabs needed watching. The controls had to be fixed.
gao-gaoreports-b-297398: Crane & Company took its January 2006 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Every challenger gets the full fair-play hearing.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-98: The Valles Caldera trust was making some progress in 2005, and GAO's report says more was needed to meet statutory goals. The findings balance credit and need. The report warns that the New Mexico preserve deserved its promised care. The goals had to be met.
gao-gaoreports-gao-05-898: Swamp swap deals lacked real watchdogs in 2005, and GAO's report says the Corps had no good way to check the trades. The findings demand the oversight. The report warns that the marshes deserved real replacement. The marshes deserved real replacement.
openalex-w7204196198: Is the world ruled by no one, or by a hidden hierarchy? This international-relations paper stages the debate between anarchic and hierarchical visions of world order. The authors work through the theories, from Waltz to the neorealists, testing which picture fits. Dense but rewarding, it tackles how scholars imagine power among nations.
openalex-w7204207398: Kidney patients die most often of heart disease, and the damage starts silently. This study looks at blood markers tied to early, hidden heart remodeling in chronic kidney disease. The authors search for signals that flag trouble before symptoms. A cardiology-nephrology study chasing an early warning for the highest-risk patients.
openalex-w7204212698: Children in institutional care carry broken bonds into the classroom. This article studies how ruptured attachments shape the inner lives and schooling of children in shelters. The authors draw on psychology and education research. Tender and serious, it argues that learning cannot be separated from love.
openalex-w7125696198: Metabolic syndrome strains the heart, and faulty temperature control may add to the load. This study asked patients how well their bodies regulate heat and linked it to heart symptom burden. The authors explored an overlooked connection. A cardiology study of the thermostat's role in heart strain.
openalex-w7221083398: Bad leg arteries darken heart bypass results. This study compared bypass outcomes in patients with severe limb ischemia against those without it. The team tracked early and late results for both groups. A heart-surgery study of two vessel diseases piling onto one patient.
arxiv-2606-15998: Search engines re-rank documents to show the most relevant ones first, often using entity labels like person or company names. This paper argues those labels do not actually signal relevance. It proposes a framework based on "observable relevance" — what the searcher can really see and use — and was presented at the 2026 ACM SIGIR conference.
arxiv-2606-16098: Bending light around corners on a chip is a core problem in photonics, especially on platforms where the refractive-index contrast is low. This paper optimizes waveguide bend designs for such materials, cutting light loss at the turns. It targets engineers building compact optical circuits on low-contrast platforms.
arxiv-2606-16598: Chill atoms in light jails can ape weird stuff — guard-edge phases and all. This look-back rounds up how such chill packs ape those phases, in lab and in math. A door-opener for new hands who'd steer chill-atom fakes. Old hands may skim for gaps.
